deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is writing out Hermann Weyl's majorant theorem for compact operators. The goal is to compare the eigenvalues λ_i of a compact operator u with its singular values ρ_i, the eigenvalues of (u*u)^{1/2}. The previous page set up an abstract principle. Take two decreasing sequences (ρ_i), (σ_i) of nonnegative reals with multiplicative majorization: ∏_1^m ρ_i ≤ ∏_1^m σ_i for every m. Hypothesis a is this weak form; hypothesis b is apparently the case of positive entries with equality ∏_1^n ρ_i = ∏_1^n σ_i. Let F(r_1,…,r_n) be symmetric with F(e^{t_1},…,e^{t_n}) convex in t. Under b, F(ρ) ≤ F(σ). Under a, the same holds if F is also increasing and continuous at r_i ≥ 0 (Th. 1, 2°). This is the multiplicative (log) form of Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya/Karamata majorization.

This page specializes to separable F. Let f be a function on ρ > 0 with f(e^t) convex, and set F(ρ_1,…,ρ_n) = Σ f(ρ_i). Then F is symmetric and F(e^{t_1},…,e^{t_n}) = Σ f(e^{t_i}) is convex, so F meets the conditions of Corollary 1 under hypothesis b. If f is moreover increasing and defined and continuous at ρ = 0, F meets the conditions of Th. 1, 2° under hypothesis a. Two inequalities follow:
- (13) Σ_1^n f(ρ_i) ≤ Σ_1^n f(σ_i).
- (14) Σ_1^k f(ρ_i) ≤ Σ_1^k f(σ_i) for k = 1,…,n, obtained under b using the earlier remark by applying the result to truncated sequences.

Example: f(ρ) = ρ^p with p real. Then f(e^t) = e^{pt} is convex for every real p. It is defined, continuous at 0 and increasing exactly when p ≥ 0. This recovers (15)/(16) of the previous page.

The next page applies this with ρ_i = |λ_i| (eigenvalues) and σ_i = singular values. The multiplicative inequalities |λ_1⋯λ_k| ≤ ρ_1⋯ρ_k are Weyl's lemma. The results are Σ f(|λ_i|) ≤ Σ f(ρ_i), then Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ ‖u‖_p^p, and in particular Σ|λ_i| ≤ ‖u‖_1 for trace-class ('Fredholm') operators and (Σ|λ_i|^2)^{1/2} ≤ ‖u‖_2 for Hilbert–Schmidt operators. These are the inputs for Grothendieck's Fredholm theory.
errors: The partial-sum inequalities (14) for k < n follow from truncating to the first k terms. For the truncated sequences only the weak multiplicative inequalities hold (hypothesis a), so one needs f increasing (and, for zero entries, continuous at 0). Hence (14) is not valid 'sous b' for arbitrary f with f(e^t) convex. Grothendieck's appeal to the 'remarque précédente' presumably supplies this, and the previous page indeed restricts (16) to p ≥ 0. As written on this page, the conditions attached to (14) are imprecise.
Implicit: the sequences must be arranged in decreasing order for the majorization hypotheses to make sense. This is not restated on this page.

ideas.what: If f(e^t) is convex, then Σ f(ρ_i) ≤ Σ f(σ_i) under multiplicative majorization with equality of total products. If f is also increasing, the same holds under weak multiplicative majorization, and partial sums are controlled as well.
ideas.modern_name: Weyl's majorant theorem / log-majorization implies weak majorization of f(e^t)-convex functions (Karamata / Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya majorization inequality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Weyl (1949), building on Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya (1929/1934) and Karamata (1932); also Pólya (1950)
ideas.where_published: Weyl's inequalities are used and stated in Grothendieck's 'Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires' (Mem. AMS 16, 1955) and in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956); exact section unsure

ideas.what: Specialization f(ρ) = ρ^p: e^{pt} is convex for every real p, and increasing and continuous at 0 iff p ≥ 0. This gives Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ Σρ_i^p.
ideas.modern_name: Weyl's inequality Σ|λ_i(u)|^p ≤ Σ s_i(u)^p (Schatten p-norm bound on eigenvalues)
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955), Chap. II (unsure of exact numbering); La théorie de Fredholm (1956)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, standard derivation of Weyl's 1949 majorant theorem in Grothendieck's own framework, preparing the eigenvalue estimates for trace-class and Hilbert–Schmidt operators that he later published. There is nothing beyond the known literature.
transcription_corrections: The annotation written under 'f(e^t) = e^{pt}' appears to read 'f(ρ)' (or 'f(r)') rather than a second 'f(e^t)'.
Struck words after 'symétrique' are illegible; 'des lignes' is doubtful.

'Prenons p.ex., [-p quelc-] {+p réel quelconque+}': the inserted text is written above the line ('p réel quelconque') and '(ρ>0)' is inserted above after ρ^p. This is consistent with the transcription.
